craft_notes: Sthāyin: kalā born — yoke, swell, twist. Rows: birth, swelling, twisting. Read aloud: cradle to crown.

lines: Māyā bore kalā, which yokes the sleeping pearl
with acting at all; and she, swelling as she does
as the world's seed — from Māyā and spirit their congress,
though risen, she twists Māyā the changeless,
but not the changeless spirit — so she is Māyā's fruit.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra māyātaḥ kalā jātā yā suptasthānīyam aṇuṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvena yunakti sā ca ucchūnateva saṃsārabījasya māyāṇvor ubhayoḥ saṃyogāt utpannāpi māyāṃ vikaroti na avikāryam aṇum iti māyākāryatvam asyāḥ
